docs.D01_business_overview.md:
Title: Ratings, benchmarks, commodity intelligence and financial workflows
Source: compiled from: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/64040/000006404026000007/a4q2025earningsrelease.htm; https://www.spglobal.com/content/dam/spglobal/corporate/en/annual-reports/2025/annual-report-2025.pdf
Date: 2026-03-18

S&P Global sells financial information, ratings, indices, commodity intelligence and mobility data. It is not a single desktop-software business. Different divisions earn revenue through subscriptions, transaction activity, benchmark licensing, asset-linked fees and other arrangements, with different exposure to issuance cycles and technology substitution.

Ratings benefits from established acceptance among issuers, investors and financial institutions. Its role depends on credibility, regulatory frameworks and market conventions. AI can assist analysis, but generating a plausible credit opinion is not the same as producing a rating recognized throughout the capital-markets ecosystem.

Indices licenses benchmark intellectual property used by investment products and market participants. Revenue can vary with assets, flows and trading, while benchmark adoption creates switching and coordination costs. Energy, including Platts, provides commodity information and reference assessments embedded in trading and commercial workflows.

Market Intelligence includes financial datasets and workflow tools. This division has more direct exposure to the concern that AI interfaces can replace research tasks or reduce demand for seats. That risk should be quantified separately from the value of licensed underlying data.

Mobility is a separate business slated for a mid-2026 separation. At this March cutoff the spin is a planned event, not a completed corporate action. Its revenues, costs and separation effects remain part of the current reporting framework.

Q4 revenue illustrates the mix: Market Intelligence $1.264 billion, Ratings $1.187 billion, Energy $576 million, Mobility $444 million and Indices $498 million, before intersegment eliminations. Operating profit was respectively $235 million, $723 million, $220 million, $71 million and $330 million. These are reported segment measures, not harmonized adjusted EBITDA.

Martina Cheung is president and CEO. Management must sustain trusted content, invest in delivery and AI integration, manage costs and allocate cash. Strong benchmarks do not eliminate debt-issuance cyclicality, fee pressure or data-licensing challenges.

The moat question is therefore specific: which products derive value from unique, trusted, legally usable information and collective adoption, and which derive value from an interface that could become cheaper or redundant? Treating every dollar of revenue as equally exposed would obscure the company's actual economic structure.
docs.D02_financial_snapshot.md:
Title: Three-year profit and FCF, including minority distributions
Source: compiled from: https://www.spglobal.com/content/dam/spglobal/corporate/en/annual-reports/2025/annual-report-2025.pdf; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/64040/000006404026000007/a4q2025earningsrelease.htm
Date: 2026-03-18

Amounts are $ millions except EPS. The annual report supplies a consistent 2023–25 series. Company-defined FCF deducts distributions to noncontrolling holders as well as capex; CFO minus physical spending alone would overstate the cash attributable to common owners.

| Metric | FY2023 | FY2024 | FY2025 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Revenue | 12,497 | 14,208 | 15,336 |
| Operating profit | 4,020 | 5,580 | 6,478 |
| Reported operating margin, rounded | 32% | 39% | 42% |
| Diluted EPS | 8.23 | 12.35 | 14.66 |
| Adjusted EPS | 12.60 | 15.70 | 17.83 |
| Operating cash flow | 3,710 | 5,689 | 5,651 |
| Capex | 143 | 124 | 195 |
| Noncontrolling distributions | 280 | 287 | 321 |
| Defined FCF | 3,287 | 5,278 | 5,135 |

FY2025 revenue increased 8% and operating profit 16%. Reported operating profit includes disposition gains, severance and other items; the annual report notes $273 million gains on dispositions and $157 million employee-severance charges. Adjusted profitability should use the full company reconciliation, not only selective adjustments.

FY2025 adjusted operating margin was 50.4%, compared with reported 42.2% in the release's more precise presentation. The difference reflects meaningful amortization and other adjustments. Calling adjusted profit “cash earnings” without examining those items would be misleading.

Year-end cash/equivalents were $1.745 billion. Short-term debt was $718 million and long-term debt $12.370 billion, total $13.088 billion. Calculated net debt was $11.343 billion before other enterprise-value adjustments. Diluted weighted-average shares were 305.1 million.

The company returned $6.2 billion in 2025, including $5.0 billion repurchases and $1.2 billion dividends. It describes that as 113% of adjusted FCF, which is not identical to the $5.135 billion unadjusted FCF in the table.

Latest Q4 revenue was $3.916 billion, up 9%. Complete quarterly cash conversion is not independently reconstructed here. A consistent ROIC series and buyback history for all three years remain missing.

The cash evidence supports a capital-efficient enterprise, but acquisition amortization, minority economics, restructuring and segment mix must remain visible when translating reported earnings into owners' cash.
docs.D03_latest_results_and_guidance.md:
Title: February10 — growth remains, but guidance disappoints expectations
Source: compiled from: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/64040/000006404026000007/a4q2025earningsrelease.htm; https://www.wsj.com/livecoverage/stock-market-today-dow-sp-500-nasdaq-02-10-2026/card/s-p-global-stock-price-sinks-dUg62l87LpnluTzWGDWM
Date: 2026-02-10

S&P Global reported Q4 revenue of $3.916 billion, up 9%, and FY2025 revenue $15.336 billion, up 8%. Full-year reported EPS was $14.66 and adjusted EPS $17.83. Adjusted operating margin was 50.4%. Strong recent profit does not resolve the market's question about the next earnings trajectory.

Management's 2026 adjusted outlook calls for organic constant-currency revenue growth of 6–8% and EPS $19.40–19.65. It projects $215–225 million capital expenditure and 10–35 basis points operating-margin expansion. The pack does not substitute a later revised outlook.

The Wall Street Journal's February10 account gives analyst consensus of $20.02 EPS before the announcement. Guidance midpoint $19.525 is approximately 2.5% below that figure, calculated. The miss is against expectations, not a forecast of an absolute EPS decline from 2025.

Management expects Mobility separation in mid-2026 and says GAAP 2026 guidance will be provided on completion. The adjusted guidance and its separation assumptions should not be confused with a fully comparable post-spin GAAP forecast. No completed separation belongs in this March information set.

The Q4 segment table demonstrates differing economics. Ratings generated $723 million operating profit on $1.187 billion revenue; Indices $330 million on $498 million; Energy $220 million on $576 million. Market Intelligence generated $235 million on $1.264 billion, while Mobility generated $71 million on $444 million.

Those reported figures show that revenue share and operating-profit share are different. The largest revenue division is not necessarily the dominant source of profit. They also do not establish the precise profit exposed to AI replacement within any division.

2025 capital return was $6.2 billion, including $5.0 billion repurchases. Buybacks can support EPS growth, but should be evaluated against debt, valuation and operating reinvestment. They are not a substitute for maintaining customer value.

A complete call-level AI-product discussion and precise subproduct recurring-revenue schedule were not independently extracted. Current analysis should therefore use verified segment evidence and explicit scenarios, with conservative sensitivity ranges for vulnerable products rather than an unsupported exact exposure percentage.

The forward test is whether benchmark and data economics can continue compounding while workflow interfaces change and debt issuance remains cyclical.
docs.D04_price_and_valuation.md:
Title: March31 — a discounted multiple requires a defined earnings base
Source: compiled from: https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/SPGI/history/?period1=1774915200&period2=1775001600; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/64040/000006404026000007/a4q2025earningsrelease.htm; https://www.spglobal.com/content/dam/spglobal/corporate/en/annual-reports/2025/annual-report-2025.pdf
Date: 2026-03-31

SPGI closed March31 at $402.40, on 2,127,530 shares in the recovered historical row. The day's low was $394.52 and high $403.89. This dated price is separated from the provider's present-day quote.

Using 305.1 million FY2025 diluted weighted-average shares gives a calculated equity-value proxy of $122.772 billion. Adding $11.343 billion calculated net debt gives an EV proxy of $134.115 billion. These are not exact cutoff values because shares and debt/cash come from older reporting dates.

| Calculated valuation | Result |
|---|---:|
| Price / FY2025 reported EPS $14.66 | 27.4x |
| Price / FY2025 adjusted EPS $17.83 | 22.6x |
| Price / 2026 guided adjusted midpoint $19.525 | 20.6x |
| FY2025 defined FCF / equity proxy | 4.2% |
| EV / FY2025 reported operating profit | 20.7x |

The forward ratio uses management guidance, not an authenticated cutoff consensus. The guidance's treatment of the planned Mobility separation requires care. A later post-spin per-share denominator cannot be inserted into March without reconciliation.

The FCF yield uses $5.135 billion after capex and noncontrolling distributions. An adjusted-FCF yield would differ. The enterprise-value ratio uses EBIT, not EBITDA; reported earnings include acquisition-related and nonrecurring items.

The February10 Journal account reports a $401.08 close after a 9.7% one-day decline, the lowest close since November2023. March31 is close to that already-public dislocation level, but a complete rolling 52-week range and daily historical multiple distribution were not authenticated.

A reliable historical comparison requires the correct price, adjusted earnings forecast and observation date, consistently measured across periods. Apparent discounts are not meaningful if the business perimeter or accounting denominator changes. The pack also lacks a harmonized cutoff Moody's/MSCI multiple table and same-date S&P500 forward P/E.

Liquidity appears substantial from the recovered volume, but a large position still requires reasonable participation and an exit plan. The economic question is whether this price compensates for workflow disruption, issuance cyclicality and transition costs while allowing durable benchmark/data franchises to compound. A lower multiple alone does not establish that outcome.
docs.D05_market_worries.md:
Title: AI substitution fears meet a lower-than-expected forecast
Source: compiled from: https://money.usnews.com/investing/news/articles/2026-02-10/s-p-global-forecasts-2026-profit-below-estimates-shares-plunge; https://www.reuters.com/business/media-telecom/global-software-stocks-hit-by-anthropic-wake-up-call-ai-disruption-2026-02-04/; https://www.wsj.com/livecoverage/stock-market-today-dow-sp-500-nasdaq-02-10-2026/card/s-p-global-stock-price-sinks-dUg62l87LpnluTzWGDWM
Date: 2026-02-10

Reuters' February10 report, syndicated by US News, describes SPGI's forecast below Wall Street expectations amid growing unease over AI disruption in software and services. It notes that financial-data and analytics businesses were swept into the broader technology selloff.

Reuters' February4 account describes nearly $1 trillion erased from software and services stocks as investors debated the implications of Anthropic's advances. The market concern is that AI agents can perform research, analysis or workflow tasks previously sold as dedicated software or professional information services.

The Journal's February10 report gives a concrete earnings comparison: adjusted guidance $19.40–19.65 versus $20.02 consensus. Shares fell 9.7% to $401.08, and Moody's fell 6.8%. This combines company-specific guidance disappointment with a broader narrative, rather than proving either factor explains the entire move.

The serious bear mechanism is loss of pricing power or seats in financial workflows, cheaper access to substitute data, and changed distribution economics as AI becomes the user's interface. Even if underlying data remains useful, a platform could retain less of the economics if intermediaries control the customer relationship.

Counterarguments must also be specific. Ratings and benchmarks depend on collective adoption, credibility and legally usable information, not just text generation. Commodity reference data has commercial and institutional use beyond a generic chatbot answer. The current segment profit table helps identify which pools matter.

Issuance cyclicality is independent of AI. A slower capital-markets environment can reduce ratings activity even if the rating franchise remains intact. Asset-linked index revenue can also vary with market levels, and regulatory pressure can affect fees or business practices.

The planned Mobility separation adds execution and comparability risk. A cleaner business mix may help, but separation costs and changed per-share financials should not be ignored.

The pack has no independently verified cutoff estimate of exactly how much consolidated revenue or profit is replaceable by AI. The affected profit pools therefore require explicit product-by-product estimation and sensitivity testing. A responsible underwriting should show base/downside adoption, pricing and retention assumptions, while distinguishing changes in delivery from loss of proprietary content value.
docs.D06_peer_and_industry_benchmarks.md:
Title: Moody's and MSCI separate benchmark economics from generic software
Source: compiled from: https://s203.q4cdn.com/694693571/files/doc_financials/2025/Annual/MOODYS-CORP_AR_BOOKMARK_2026_V1-Reduced.pdf; https://ir.msci.com/news-releases/news-release-details/msci-reports-financial-results-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/64040/000006404026000007/a4q2025earningsrelease.htm
Date: 2026-02-26

Moody's is the closest public ratings/data comparison; MSCI is a useful index and analytics comparison. Neither matches all SPGI divisions, so corporate multiple comparisons require attention to mix and earnings adjustments.

Moody's 2025 report gives revenue approximately $7.7 billion, up 9%, and adjusted operating margin 51.1%, up 300 basis points. Reported EPS was $13.67 and adjusted EPS $14.94, up 21% and 20% respectively. Those are annual company figures, not the preliminary search snippet's mislabeled EPS series.

MSCI's January28 Q4 release reports revenue $822.5 million, up 10.6%, with organic growth 10.2%. Recurring subscription revenue increased 7.5% and asset-based fees 20.7%. Operating margin was 56.4%, adjusted EBITDA margin 62.2%, and adjusted EPS $4.66, up approximately11%.

SPGI's FY2025 adjusted operating margin was 50.4%, while reported margin was 42.2%. Directly comparing it to MSCI's EBITDA margin would be wrong because depreciation, amortization and other adjustments differ. The peer evidence nevertheless demonstrates high margins and recurring/benchmark economics.

The shared moat is not simply software code. Recognized ratings, adopted benchmarks, trusted datasets and embedded customer processes can create high switching and coordination costs. AI may alter the interface without automatically recreating all institutional acceptance or data rights.

The shared risk is that customers demand lower prices or different licensing as AI expands access. Benchmark licensing and proprietary inputs may retain value while desktop or seat-based products face pressure. Moody's and MSCI are not immune merely because they have familiar brand names.

Current operating growth is counterevidence to a claim of already-observed wholesale displacement. It does not settle long-run economics. Issuance cycles, market-sensitive asset fees and client budgets can weaken even without technology disruption.

Exact March31 peer forward EPS, multiples and harmonized FCF yields were not authenticated. No precise relative-value ranking is supplied. The useful benchmark is the combination of recurring revenue, profit margins and distinct contractual/IP economics, which should be compared with the actual threatened SPGI products rather than with generic software-sector sentiment.
docs.D07_event_timeline.md:
Title: The guidance and AI-disruption chronology through March
Source: compiled from: https://www.reuters.com/business/media-telecom/global-software-stocks-hit-by-anthropic-wake-up-call-ai-disruption-2026-02-04/; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/64040/000006404026000007/a4q2025earningsrelease.htm; https://www.wsj.com/livecoverage/stock-market-today-dow-sp-500-nasdaq-02-10-2026/card/s-p-global-stock-price-sinks-dUg62l87LpnluTzWGDWM; https://www.spglobal.com/content/dam/spglobal/corporate/en/annual-reports/2025/annual-report-2025.pdf; https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/SPGI/history/?period1=1774915200&period2=1775001600
Date: 2026-03-31

During 2025: SPGI's businesses grew, with full-year revenue ultimately reaching $15.336 billion. Ratings, indices and commodity information remained distinct profit pools alongside Market Intelligence and Mobility. A planned Mobility separation would change the reporting perimeter, but had not completed by this cutoff.

January2026: Competitor MSCI reported growth in both subscriptions and asset-based fees. That public evidence offers an industry benchmark before the sharp February sentiment shift.

February4: Reuters described a broad software/services rout following concern about Anthropic's rapidly advancing AI capabilities. Financial-information providers were included in the debate about tasks, interfaces and customer spending.

February10: SPGI reported FY2025 revenue growth8%, adjusted EPS$17.83 and 2026 guidance$19.40–19.65. The range fell below the reported$20.02 consensus. Management expected6–8% organic constant-currency revenue growth and modest operating-margin expansion.

The same day: Shares fell9.7% to$401.08 according to the Journal, the lowest close since November2023. Moody's fell6.8%, showing that the reaction extended beyond SPGI's particular guidance. The price event does not identify how much each causal factor contributed.

February18–26: Moody's released and documented strong2025 annual results, including$7.7billion revenue and51.1% adjusted operating margin. The continued industry profitability is relevant counterevidence, not proof that future disruption is impossible.

March18: SPGI's annual report provided full2025 financial statements and historical cash-flow reconciliation. The FCF definition deducts minority distributions in addition to capex, a material detail for valuation.

March31: Shares closed$402.40. This is the conservative pre-Q2 review date. Exact investor execution dates remain outside the public company evidence, and no later quarter or completed spin is included.

The question now is whether a de-rated valuation overstates disruption of trusted benchmark/data economics or instead anticipates a durable change in how customers purchase and use information. The answer requires mapping the threatened products to revenue, profit and cash, rather than projecting a broad sector narrative onto every division.

The planned separation also requires keeping comparable reporting perimeters explicit.
docs.D08_pershing_context.md:
Title: Concentration, capital and the standard for an information franchise
Source: compiled from: https://assets.pershingsquareholdings.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/11144917/2026-Annual-Investor-Presentation.pdf; https://assets.pershingsquareholdings.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/15162701/PSH-Fact-Sheet-December-2025-Website.pdf
Date: 2026-02-11

February9 gross core-fund AUM was$19.748billion and core equity$16.077billion, disclosed February11. PSH gross assets were$17.872billion and equity$14.202billion. Howard Hughes-inclusive gross assets of$30.040billion are a different perimeter, not incremental liquid fund cash.

The presentation identifies December31 capital weights of Amazon13%, Meta10% and Hertz2%. Public core franchises also include Alphabet, Brookfield, Uber, Universal Music, Restaurant Brands, Howard Hughes and Fannie/Freddie exposure. Complete exact March allocations and uncommitted cash are unavailable.

The fact sheet describes a concentrated portfolio, usually8–12 core liquid large-cap businesses, and limited annual new-name turnover. An ordinary US13F table omits foreign, OTC and some derivative assets, so its percentages cannot be assumed to be full-fund NAV weights.

The public investment framework emphasizes predictable FCF, durable entry barriers, capable management, strong financial profiles and limited dependence on external funding. SPGI should be tested through trusted benchmarks, data rights, customer retention and cash conversion rather than a generalized label such as “high-quality information.”

High accounting margins are not sufficient. The investor must determine whether current products remain indispensable, whether AI changes only delivery or also pricing power, and whether the forecast survives weaker issuance and market levels. Minority distributions and debt must remain part of owner-cash analysis.

The portfolio already owns technology-enabled franchises exposed to AI narratives. An information provider might add a different revenue model while increasing sensitivity to similar valuation and disruption debates. Correlation should be checked economically rather than only through sector classifications.

No authenticated current SPGI-specific Ackman thesis statement dated by March31 is included. Earlier familiarity with a company does not establish today's decision, cost basis or forecast. This pack contains current public evidence, not a later investment explanation.

The appropriate hurdle is prospective return from the present price under a defensible distribution of outcomes. A large multiple decline can create opportunity, but it cannot substitute for confidence in data/benchmark durability. Permanent capital supports patience only when the underlying long-term economics remain underwritable.

drivers.driver: Ratings, Indices and Platts dominate earnings and possess durable benchmark/oligopoly advantages.
The AI-threatened desktop exposure was small relative to the enterprise profit pool.
Proprietary structured data can become more valuable within AI workflows.
Growth and capital return were available at about19x earnings versus about25x before de-rating.

answer_key.pack_quality_notes: 8 documents, three-year annual financial/cash series, minority FCF deductions, segment profit mapping, primary guidance and dated AI/guidance press. March31pre-Q2 freeze avoids unknown firstday. Later July spin completion and August >80%profit/<7%desktop-revenue claims excluded from docs. Exact historical/52week multiple series, peerforward valuations and subproduct threat estimates missing. Driver quotes null because primary wording beyond compendium was not independently verified; no invented quotations.

valuation.eps_path: 8% annual growth driven by 6-8% organic revenue growth, margin expansion, and share repurchases
valuation.downside_case: Multiple compression to 16x and earnings stagnation resulting in a 20% loss over 3 years

drivers.driver: The company is a dominant, high-margin information services franchise with powerful network effects and significant free cash flow generation [D01, D03].
We were able to acquire our stake at 20.6x forward earnings, a valuation that discounts the company's long-term durable growth trajectory [D03, D04].
Management demonstrates strong shareholder alignment through aggressive capital returns, having repurchased $5.0 billion in shares in 2025 [D02].
The market's concern regarding AI disruption is misplaced, as the company’s data products are mission-critical and protected by deep-seated regulatory and network moats [D01, D05].

kill_criteria: Structural decline in ratings market share due to new regulatory or AI-enabled competitors
Organic revenue growth falls below 4% for consecutive quarters
Leverage ratio increases significantly beyond historical norms
Management shifts capital allocation away from substantial share repurchases toward dilutive, non-core M&A
final.what_would_change_our_mind: Evidence that AI-driven automation is commoditizing the company's research and ratings products, leading to a permanent impairment of pricing power and market share.
final.memo:
The Company is a dominant, high-margin information services provider that occupies a mission-critical role in global capital markets [D01]. Through its ratings, indices, and data segments, the business benefits from powerful network effects and regulatory barriers that make it remarkably simple and predictable [D01, D06]. With a 50.4% adjusted operating margin and minimal maintenance capex, the company is a prolific generator of free cash flow [D02, D03].

We are taking advantage of a market dislocation that has caused the shares to trade at a 20.6x forward P/E multiple [D03, D04]. The market has incorrectly conflated temporary cyclicality in debt issuance with a structural decline, while overreacting to AI-related fears and a minor discrepancy in near-term EPS guidance [D03, D05]. We believe these fears are transitory and do not reflect the durability of the company’s 6-8% organic revenue growth [D03].

Our entry valuation of 20.6x 2026 earnings offers an attractive rate of return, with a path toward mid-teens earnings growth [D03, D04]. Given the strength of the business, we view a return to a 22x historical multiple as a conservative target [D03, D04]. Over a three-year horizon, this provides an expected IRR of approximately 21% under our base case assumptions [D03].

Management has proven to be excellent stewards of capital, returning $6.2 billion to shareholders in 2025 alone, including $5.0 billion in repurchases [D02]. We expect this aggressive capital return strategy to continue, serving as a primary catalyst for value realization [D02, D03]. We do not require active engagement to unlock this value, as the existing strategy is sound and shareholder-aligned [D02, D04].

Risks remain, particularly regarding the potential for AI-driven automation to disrupt financial research and data demands [D05]. However, given the high barriers to entry and the sticky, mission-critical nature of these franchises, we believe our downside is bounded [D01, D03]. Should evidence emerge that these moats are eroding, we will reconsider our position [D05].

We are initiating a position today with a target size of 10% of NAV. This allocation reflects our high conviction in the quality of the franchise and the durability of its growth profile, notwithstanding current market sentiment [D02, D08].

valuation.downside_case: Multiple contraction to 15-17x if AI significantly commoditizes research and issuance remains depressed.

drivers.driver: S&P Global is a dominant financial utility with high barriers to entry via entrenched network effects in credit ratings and indices [D01, D06].
The business is highly free-cash-flow-generative with 50.4% adjusted operating margins and disciplined capital allocation [D02, D03].
The market has mispriced the stock due to a temporary guidance miss and overblown fears regarding AI disruption of its research and data offerings [D03, D05].
The company maintains a strong growth outlook of 6-8% organic revenue growth driven by the secular demand for financial data [D03].

kill_criteria: Structural decline in operating margins below 45% indicating loss of pricing power.
Organic revenue growth turns negative for two consecutive quarters.
Material loss of market share in credit ratings or indices due to competitive disruption or regulatory changes.
Management shifts from shareholder-friendly capital allocation to debt-funded, low-return acquisitions.
final.what_would_change_our_mind: Evidence that AI-driven technological shifts commoditize the company's research and data offerings, permanently eroding its competitive moat and pricing power.
final.memo:
S&P Global is an essential financial infrastructure provider, operating as a dominant, high-margin, and free-cash-flow-generative franchise [D01, D02]. The company’s ratings and indices businesses benefit from high switching and coordination costs, creating a durable competitive moat that is difficult for competitors to replicate [D01, D06]. With a 50.4% adjusted operating margin and significant recurring revenue, the business generates the predictable, high-quality cash flow that defines our standard for a core compounder [D02, D03].

We are able to acquire our stake at a 20.6x forward P/E, a valuation that we believe understates the long-term compounding potential of the firm [D03, D04]. The opportunity arises from a 9.7% share price decline following a short-term guidance miss, which the market has incorrectly extrapolated as a structural impairment to growth [D03, D05]. We view this dislocation as a classic opportunity to buy a great business that is underperforming its potential for fixable or temporary reasons [D03].

Our investment thesis is predicated on the firm’s ability to sustain 6–8% organic revenue growth, supported by the secular demand for financial intelligence [D03]. By maintaining ~50% operating margins and continuing to deploy capital into share repurchases—which totaled $5 billion in 2025—we expect the company to deliver attractive mid-teens annual rates of return [D02, D03]. We anticipate a re-rating toward a 22x terminal multiple as the company demonstrates the resilience of its moat against AI and confirms the durability of its growth profile [D02, D03, D06].

As long-term owners, our role is to support the management team in their continued focus on capital allocation and operational execution [D02]. We identify S&P Global as a high-quality compounder that fits perfectly within our 3.0 era mandate of acquiring dominant utilities during periods of market sentiment weakness. We are initiating a position today with a target of 10% of NAV [D04, D05].
